subject: Localized Cloud Peering Failure: Immediate Reroute Steps & After-Action Plan
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: ops@brightcart.com, support@brightcart.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Localized Cloud Peering Failure: Immediate Reroute Steps & After-Action Plan

Hi Alice / BrightCart ops team —

Quick note to confirm we detected a peering blackout at one of our cloud provider’s exchange points that impacted egress/ingress to several Redwood edge POPs serving the US-East, EU-West and APAC-SIN regions. BigCloud has acknowledged the issue (status@bigcloudstatus.com) and is routing mitigation, but they’ve estimated 2–5 hours for full convergence earlier this morning.

Impact observed: elevated connection failures and increased tail latency for a subset of requests originating in the three regions above; some requests failed to negotiate TLS at the edge and fell back to retries. We’ve already triggered our automatic fallback routing, but we expect a short window of elevated error rates while caches warm on alternate paths.

Immediate action we recommend for BrightCart (minimal change, fast cutover):
- Update endpoint preference to regional-fallback-1 (us-east/fallback-1, eu-west/fallback-1, apac-sin/fallback-1) — this is a DNS-prefixed preference we control and will route your traffic to Hot Standby nodes.
- If you prefer an IP-based change, switch outbound to 34.120.19.45 (us) / 52.87.34.11 (eu) / 13.250.12.96 (apac) for the next 4 hours.
- Short-term config window: we suggest a 15–30 minute maintenance window for cutover to validate connection success and token exchange.

I attached a condensed reroute-playbook (reroute-playbook.pdf) with step-by-step CLI and dashboard checks. Vanessa is on-call for execution and will coordinate with your SREs. Please confirm an ETA for cutover and whether you want us to run the DNS flip from our side.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll follow up with a full after-action once BigCloud provides their remediation timeline.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — I’ll be your POC for the cutover and I’ll stay on the BrightCart Slack channel (#brightcart-ops) while we run the steps. To answer your questions: 
- Session affinity: the fallback nodes preserve token validation and session affinity for signed tokens; long-lived web sockets may reconnect and get a new socket id, but auth/refresh flows are unaffected.
- Cost/latency delta: expect a +5–12% per-token CPU overhead while the fallback nodes handle increased KV cache misses; median latency change usually ~+20–60ms for the path switch. We will monitor costs and can roll back immediately if you prefer.
- Ramp plan: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 10 minutes is reasonable. We’ll warm caches by prefetching your top 50 prompts (I’ll share a pre-warm script).

If BrightCart approves, I’ll run the DNS flip at 09:00 PT and post progress every 5 minutes.

Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Post-incident summary: localized peering failure (Jun 11) — next steps and draft postmortem

Hi Alice and BrightCart team —

Thanks again for working with us during the June 11 peering failure. Below is a short summary and next steps; I’ve attached the postmortem draft (postmortem-draft.md) and the traffic metrics we collected during the event (traffic-metrics.csv). If you’d like any edits before we publish, let me know — we will not publish externally until BrightCart signs off.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2028-06-11 07:48–11:12 PT (root cause: third-party exchange BGP flap at BigCloud POP; BigCloud’s remediation was BGP path dampening and re-advertisement).
- Impact: elevated request errors and higher median p95 latency across us-east, eu-west, apac-sin for ~3.5 hours; automatic fallback reduced customer-visible errors by ~78% compared to no fallback.
- Mitigation performed: DNS-based endpoint preference flip and stepwise traffic ramp (25/50/100); pre-warm script to reduce cold KV misses; manual monitoring and automated scaling.
- Outcome: traffic normalized within 30 minutes of full ramp; no data loss or token compromise observed.

Recommended follow-ups (we’d like to align with BrightCart):
1) Approve the postmortem for joint publication (we’ll redact internal-only logs).
2) Confirm whether you want a one-time service credit for the impacted window (Ben — can you advise next steps and computation using DEAL-47829?).
3) Operational: we recommend adding a provider-peering diversion runbook to your runbook set (we can co-author).

We appreciate the patience and the quick coordination from Alice and the BrightCart SREs. Please reply with any edits or the green light to publish.

Best,
Markus Klein
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
